claude.sample_unit: prospective test samples for BCL prediction (116 for NVF)

links.outcome: LLM predictive performance versus traditional ML models and surgeons on same data
links.effect: LLMs comparable to TML for BCL (F1 0.857-0.871 vs 0.758-0.867) but worse for NVF zero-shot (F1 0.309 vs RBF-SVM 0.536); LLMs did not outperform TML models.
links.quote: The LLMs did not outperform the TML models in the domain-specific tasks.

links.outcome: Surgeon prediction performance with versus without LLM predictions and explanations
links.effect: BCL: surgeon F1 rose from 0.675-0.684 to 0.724-0.752; NVF: subtle contrary changes, Surgeon 1 F1 0.310 to 0.370-0.409, Surgeon 2 0.322 to 0.308-0.315.
links.quote: After consultation of the predictions and interpretations from either LLMs, their performances showed subtle but contrary change that F1 score slightly increased to 0.370–0.409 and MCC to 0.185–0.266 for Surgeon 1 , while the numbers slightly decreased to 0.308–0.315 and 0.061–0.077 for Surgeon 2 .

links.outcome: Clinician performance when assisted by LLM output versus unassisted
links.effect: LLM assistance improved surgeon BCL prediction (F1 0.739-0.752 vs 0.684 for Surgeon 1) but gave no consistent benefit for NVF.
links.quote: Whether the decision-support value of output from LLMs demonstrated highly depend on model’s overall accuracy and reliability on the task.

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM outputs across three repeated runs
links.effect: Gwet's AC1 0.856-0.994 for zero-shot and 0.730-0.850 for few-shot, indicating perfect to substantial consistency.
links.quote: ChatGPT and DeepSeek exhibited equally perfect consistency in three-time repeat responses for zero-shot prediction (Gwet’s AC1, 0.856–0.994) and substantial-to-perfect consistency for few-shot prediction (Gwet’s AC1, 0.730–0.850; Supplementary Table 3 ).

links.outcome: LLM prediction accuracy against ground-truth outcomes
links.effect: Zero-shot LLMs predicted all samples would develop NVF (100% vs 18% actual); NVF F1 0.309, MCC 0.044; subtype prediction poor.
links.quote: For example, both LLMs under zero-shot prompting predicted all samples would develop NVF, far more than the actual occurrence rate (100% vs. 18%), for which nearly all LLMs’ explanation highlighted low BMD as the primary determining factor.

links.effect: Zero-shot LLMs showed high sensitivity and low specificity (<0.500); NVF specificity 0.011-0.071 with sensitivity ~1.0.
links.quote: However, they were extremely unbalanced, exhibiting high sensitivity and low specificity (<0.500), thereby reducing their clinical utility.

unlisted_practices: Few-shot prompting with in-context examples to improve LLM specificity in prognostic prediction

openai.sample_unit: patients for BCL prediction; NVF analysis subset had 483 patients

links.outcome: LLM performance versus TML models and surgeons
links.effect: BCL: zero-shot LLM F1 0.857/0.871 vs TML F1 0.766–0.836. NVF: zero-shot LLM F1 0.309/MCC 0.044; RBF-SVM F1 0.514/MCC 0.414.
links.quote: They did not outperform the TML models in these domain-specific tasks.
LLM explanations enhanced surgeon performance in BCL prediction but not in NVF.

links.effect: NVF zero-shot F1-score 0.309 and MCC 0.044; few-shot improved, but overall gains were uncertain.
links.quote: For NVF prediction, the zero-shot LLM performance was poor (F1-score, 0.309; MCC, 0.044) but improved with few-shot learning.

links.effect: Zero-shot Gwet’s AC1 0.856–0.994; few-shot Gwet’s AC1 0.730–0.850.
links.quote: ChatGPT and DeepSeek exhibited equally perfect consistency in three-time repeat responses for zero-shot prediction (Gwet’s AC1, 0.856–0.994) and substantial-to-perfect consistency for few-shot prediction (Gwet’s AC1, 0.730–0.850; Supplementary Table 3 ).

unlisted_practices: Few-shot prompting with outcome-stratified real-world examples to improve LLM prognostic prediction

models_evaluated: Support Vector Machine with Radial Basis Function Kernel

links.outcome: predictive performance of LLMs compared to traditional machine learning models
links.effect: LLMs did not outperform TML models; RBF-SVM had highest F1 (0.514) and MCC (0.414) for NVF, while TML models had superior MCCs (0.384–0.416) for BCL
links.quote: The LLMs did not outperform the TML models in the domain-specific tasks.
